subject: tulipindicators x C2SaferRust (laertes_benchmarks/tulipindicators_WIP), CLI-level defects: argc off-by-one in main() wrapper (bug 2) + zero-arg NULL argv[1] SIGSEGV (bug 1)

corpus.generator: SEEDED GENERATOR (random.seed(42)) -- NOT coverage-guided; libFuzzer is not the natural mechanism at a CLI boundary
corpus.decoding: byte0 = indicator index into indicators.txt (mod 104; 0xFF = no args); byte1 = k options (mod 5); next k bytes -> option value b%20+1 as decimal argv strings
corpus.composition: 2 canonical (000: no args; 001: sma 5) + 104 one-per-indicator + 96 random-indicator records, k uniform in 0..4

boundary: process/CLI. O-R = CLI exit code (ret line in state file), O-P = (wrapper exit code, forwarded stdout), O-S = O-R (no designated output memory at a CLI boundary; globals:none), O-F = O-S U O-P
ub_gate: C sample under -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all, halt_on_error=1 exitcode=99; input excluded iff sanitizer report on stderr / exit 99 / signal (>=128) / timeout. C exit 1 (usage error) is NOT UB and stays a valid record (cell-specific patch of replay.py). Repeated C replay for C-unstable.
what_did_not_work: First run: C 'hma 1 4' hit a real ASan global-buffer-overflow, but ASAN_OPTIONS=abort_on_error=1 hung after the report; wrapper's 20 s timeout raised an uncaught TimeoutExpired -> no state file, no sanitizer text reached replay.py, record slipped past the gate as a bogus semantic-difference. Fix: halt_on_error=1:exitcode=99 (no abort), wrapper catches timeout -> exit 137 + '[TIMEOUT]' on stderr, gate also keys on rc==99/[TIMEOUT]. Rerun: that record is now C-UB (excluded).

Generic replay.py treats C rc!=0 as UB and Rust rc!=0 as Rust-failure; both wrong at a CLI boundary (exit 1 = usage error is the normal return). Patched copy in harness/replay.py: C gate = sanitizer/signal/timeout only; Rust-failure = signal or panic(101) only.
